- File: scripts/pr6576_shard_followup.py
  Line or code reference: `_clean_old_entry()` (around line 400-406), specifically `int(entry["rc"])` and `int(entry["tests"])`; also `int(group["group"])` in `clean_old_results()` at line 423.
  Problem: The old-head artifact comes from an untrusted runner that executes PR #6576's historical code. The coerced integers are unbounded: Python 3.12 accepts integers up to thousands of digits, and `build_report()` renders them verbatim into the GitHub comment body (`| {int(group['group'])} | {shard_index} | {int(shard['tests'])} | {int(shard['rc'])} | … |`). A single oversized integer (or an artifact that smuggles one into the field) could push the body past GitHub's 65536-char limit and cause the `report` POST to fail, which means the one-time marker never lands and the workflow re-runs on every subsequent push. `clean_old_results()` already iterates a bounded subset (`raw["groups"][:GROUPS]`, `group["shards"][:SHARDS]`), but the field values inside that subset are unchecked.
  Why it fails at runtime: With the worst-case shard count (16 rows × ~10 fields), a single 4000-char integer cell already pushes the body to 60-70K characters. The `report` POST then fails, the marker is never posted, and every later `main` push re-enters `locate` → `rerun` → `report` instead of short-circuiting at the `guard` step.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

- File: scripts/pr6576_shard_followup.py
  Line or code reference: `_start()` line 322: `env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not re.search(r"(TOKEN|SECRET|_PAT|API_KEY)$", k)}`.
  Problem: The deny-list regex relies on suffix tokens and would miss credentials exposed under non-matching names (e.g. `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, or any future credential-bearing env var added by the runner image). The subprocess env is otherwise copied verbatim.
  Why it fails at runtime: On a runner image change (or a custom Actions runner) that introduces a credential-bearing env var under a non-suffix-matching name, that value would be inherited by the test-code subprocess and could be exfiltrated through stdout/file writes. The mitigation requires the runner image to keep credential vars under one of the four suffix patterns; nothing in this codebase enforces that.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
